title: Subnet lifecycle orchestrator and endpoint reconciliation Terraform module
creator: Ava Thompson
description: Build a single, composable Terraform module that standardizes subnet lifecycle, NAT/IGW provisioning, VPC endpoint creation, and dynamic routing rules for Private (VPC) deployments. This module will be the canonical building block used by Private deployments and the Private installer. It must: 1) support multi-AZ subnet tiling and role-based subnet classification (control, compute, inference, egress), 2) choose egress path per-subnet via policy (IGW vs NAT gateways vs Egress-only), 3) reconcile VPC endpoints (S3, STS, KMS, internal service endpoints) including cross-account endpoint policies and prefix-list attachments, 4) maintain route table lifecycle and reconcile route drift with a safe remediation plan, 5) expose canary-friendly upgrade hooks and preflight checks (terraform plan analysis + synthetic probes), and 6) surface detailed telemetry for health checks and upgrade outcomes to the Console and deploy logs.
acceptance_criteria: Module input schema documented with example usage for Hosted/Dedicated/Private installs
Module creates AZ-aware subnets with tags and maps provided subnet roles to route tables
NAT/IGW provisioning supports autoscale pattern via usage metrics and provides a stable egress IP set
VPC endpoint reconciler applies endpoint policies and validates prefix-list attachments; cross-account endpoints create proper IAM policy references
Route reconciliation detects drift and proposes a non-destructive remediation plan (human approval required for destructive changes)
Upgrade flow includes a plan-only canary mode and automated synthetic health checks (connection + DNS + S3 put/get) with pass/fail thresholds
Terratest and CI integration verify core flows: create/update/destroy for module examples (min infra), and tfsec scan passes with remediation notes
progress_updates: 2026-02-12: Initial proto module skeleton committed (subnets + tags + basic route tables). See PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/1284
2026-02-20: Added endpoint resource templates for S3 and STS; discovered cross-account policy edge-case where AWS ignores explicit deny on endpoint policy in same-account attachments
2026-02-28: Implemented route table tagging and route ownership model. Started simple drift detector that runs terraform plan and extracts 'to be created/changed' routes into a remediation proposal
2026-03-04: Wire up synthetic probe lambda (nodejs) to run S3 put/get and TCP connect tests in each AZ; hooked to module via aws_lambda_invocation data source for preflight validations
2026-03-08: First internal integration test run in staging passed for create/update flows; observed NAT gateway scaling flapping under bursty test, added stabilization backoff in autoscale policy
blockers: AWS limitation: Cannot atomically replace route table association without brief traffic shift. Need to design canary migration pattern to avoid blackhole windows
Cross-account VPC endpoint IAM binding semantics require legal/infra approval for wide-use prefix lists (security review in progress)
Terratest concurrency flakiness when running many AZs in parallel causing quota errors in shared test account
testing_plan: Unit tests for input validation and tag generation (terraform validate + tflint rules)
Integration with Terratest: create minimal VPC, apply module, verify endpoints, run synthetic lambda probes, destroy
Load-style test for NAT autoscaler: generate egress traffic ramp and assert number of NATs scales with stabilization backoff
Upgrade canary run: apply module v1 -> v2 in a single AZ, execute synthetic probes, then rollout cluster-wide
rollout_plan: 1. Merge module to infra registry (private-2026.04 branch)
2. Apply in a single non-prod region with canary AZ and run synthetic health checks for 24h
3. If canary passes, enable staged rollout per account with automated plan review and manual approval gate for destructive changes
4. Post-rollout health survey and metrics collection (Console dashboard; latency/failed-probe counts)
notes: Design trade-offs discussed: prefer explicit NAT pools per AZ (improves egress IP stability) vs shared centralized NAT (simpler but single point of failure)
We chose a reconciliation-first model: module will not auto-apply destructive route removals without explicit approval; it will mark them in the plan and expose remediation tag in Console
Operator ergonomics: provide a 'preview-remediate' script which fetches plan, runs synthetic probes, and uploads a remediation proposal to the Console for approval
